meta.title: Ondra Webhook Inbox
meta.description: Event announcement inbox for Ondra (L9 extension pool, reuse tier): it answers three questions — something just happened outside, should it be said, when should it be said, and which kind is it. The host parses a webhook into a simple event record and hands it over; this plugin does four things: deduplication (the fingerprint is a hash of source, type and the sorted key fields, so the same event is never announced twice — it is sixteen hex characters and irreversible, which is exactly why deduplication by fingerprint can never be used to reconstruct content), enqueueing (the queue has a hard cap, the oldest item is dropped when full and the log says which ones went, never a silent truncation; the fingerprint of a dropped item is dropped with it, otherwise an event that was never announced would count as already announced), quiet-hours holding (eleven at night to eight in the morning, the same window as proactive speech — during it events are enqueued but not delivered), and three-tier priority ordering (high priority only sorts earlier; it cannot bypass the enable switch and cannot pass through quiet hours — leaving an urgent-so-it-may-speak-at-night path would turn quiet hours into a suggestion). It stores summaries and fingerprints only, never originals: body, raw and payload are typed never in the contract, which is a compile-time refusal rather than an omission, and no field in the state file can reconstruct a request body. It never sends anything itself (sending belongs to the six gates), never starts an HTTP server or listens on a port (receiving webhooks and verifying signatures belong to the host — the host calls it, it does not connect to anyone), has no UI, installs no timers, and carries no message templates. Inbox, deduplication and rate limiting are mature patterns; this plugin only wires them up and configures them, introducing no dependencies and copying no code.
